title: Hopwood Hall College Unveils Ambitious Five-Year Vision at Rochdale Town Hall
excerpt: An independent assessment estimates Hopwood Hall College generated £388 million for the UK economy in 2024–25, including £57 million in Greater Manchester through college spending.
body:
An independent economic impact assessment estimates that Hopwood Hall College generated £388 million for the UK economy through its work in the 2024–25 academic year.

The report was prepared by London Economics and published in September 2026. It estimates that the college generated about £10 of economic value for every £1 spent.

The assessment attributes £299 million to the college's teaching and training activity. That estimate reflects the additional employment and earnings associated with qualifications and apprenticeships.

A further £90 million is linked to the college's wider spending. The report estimates that this supported around 820 full-time equivalent jobs across the UK, including 605 in Greater Manchester. It puts the Greater Manchester economic impact associated with that spending at £57 million.

The £388 million headline is a UK-wide estimate rather than a figure for Rochdale borough alone. The component figures have been rounded, which is why the stated £299 million and £90 million do not add precisely to the headline total.

Hopwood Hall College has campuses in Rochdale and Middleton. Its courses, apprenticeships and employer partnerships mean the findings are relevant to local learners, families and businesses considering how further education supports skills and employment across the borough.

Julia Heap OBE, principal and chief executive of Hopwood Hall College, said: “At Hopwood Hall College, we’re driven by our ambition to change lives and drive good growth.

“We are therefore delighted that this independent review demonstrates the significant economic contribution we’re making both in Rochdale and beyond.

“Behind every statistic is a person gaining new skills, an employer developing its workforce, or a local business benefiting from the economic activity we generate.

“We are incredibly proud to be an anchor institution in our communities and, as our region continues to grow and attract investment, our role in developing the skilled workforce needed to seize those opportunities has never been more important.”

The assessment was first highlighted when the college launched its five-year strategy at Rochdale Town Hall. The strategy set out plans to support growth, open new opportunities and develop the workforce needed by employers through to 2031.

The figures are estimates from economic modelling prepared for the college. Rochdale Daily has not independently recalculated them.
